title: Outlook: usage display for Recoverable Items storage
summary: The roadmap facts and the documented Exchange commands are supported. Qualify the legacy Exchange admin center path because Microsoft's cited pages disagree, add the higher Recoverable Items quotas for archived mailboxes on hold, and cover the checklist's hold and archive checks in the controls table.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Get-MailboxFolderStatistics -Identity <mailbox> -FolderScope RecoverableItems retrieves Recoverable Items folder statistics.
claims.quote: RecoverableItems: Returns output for the Recoverable Items folder and the Deletions, DiscoveryHolds, Purges, and Versions subfolders.

claims.claim: Learn recommends Get-EXOMailboxFolderStatistics instead in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: In Exchange Online PowerShell, we recommend that you use the Get-EXOMailboxFolderStatistics cmdlet instead of this cmdlet.

claims.claim: The Archive switch retrieves archive mailbox usage statistics.
claims.quote: The Archive switch specifies whether to return the usage statistics of the archive associated with the mailbox or mail user.

claims.claim: The cited article gives Exchange admin center > Compliance management > Retention policies for creating the policy containing the Recoverable Items tag.
claims.quote: In the EAC, go to Compliance management > Retention policies, and then select Add
claims.fix: Flag this as conflicting legacy guidance rather than an unqualified current portal path: the cited article gives this EAC path, but https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/security-and-compliance/recoverable-items-folder/recoverable-items-folder says Exchange security and compliance features are no longer available in the new EAC. State both.

claims.claim: The printed New-RetentionPolicyTag command creates a RecoverableItems retention tag with the specified age and MoveToArchive action.
claims.quote: New-RetentionPolicyTag -Name <Name of RPT> -Type RecoverableItems -AgeLimitForRetention <Number of days> -RetentionAction MoveToArchive

claims.claim: The Recoverable Items retention tag itself must be created with PowerShell, not the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: Use PowerShell to create an RPT for the Recoverable Items folder. You can't use the Exchange admin center (EAC).

claims.claim: Moving Recoverable Items to the archive requires an enabled archive mailbox; without it no action is taken.
claims.quote: For this process to work, the user's archive mailbox must be enabled. If the archive mailbox isn't enabled, no action is taken

claims.claim: The cited retention-policy procedure is framed for mailboxes on hold and can apply a policy to multiple mailboxes.
claims.quote: You can use the EAC or Exchange Online PowerShell to apply the retention policy to a single mailbox or to multiple mailboxes.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said the existing statistics and archiving controls govern the contents of the new display.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recoverable items storage usage display hide disable PowerShell Graph policy. Read results and opened Get-MailboxFolderStatistics and Increase the Recoverable Items quota for mailboxes on hold in eDiscovery; neither connects these controls to the new display.

claims.claim: Where in Outlook the new figure appears is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "Recoverable Items" "storage" "usage" display 579190 admin setting policy default licensing. Read results, roadmap and Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; no location for the new display stated.

claims.claim: Whether the new display covers the archive mailbox is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recoverable items storage usage visibility licensing price meter archive subfolders default rollout. Read results, roadmap and cited quota article; archive storage is documented, but its inclusion in the new display is not.

claims.claim: Recoverable Items resides in the hidden non-IPM subtree of a mailbox.
claims.quote: The Recoverable Items folder resides in the non-IPM subtree of each mailbox. This subtree isn't visible to users using Outlook, Outlook on the web (formerly known as Outlook Web App), or other email clients.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Recoverable Items stores soft-deleted items.
claims.quote: Soft-deleted items are moved to the Deletions subfolder of the Recoverable Items folder.

claims.claim: For mailboxes on hold or under a Microsoft 365 retention policy, Versions preserves copies of edited items.
claims.quote: Versions: If In-Place Hold, Litigation Hold, or a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 retention policy is enabled, this subfolder contains the original copy of the item

claims.claim: Hard-deleted items are preserved in Recoverable Items for mailboxes under applicable holds or retention policies.
claims.quote: DiscoveryHolds: Contains hard-deleted items that have been preserved by an eDiscovery hold or a retention policy.

claims.claim: Learn lists deleted item retention, single item recovery, holds, Microsoft 365 retention policies, mailbox audit logging and calendar logging as users of Recoverable Items.
claims.quote: Deleted item retention; Single item recovery; In-Place Hold; Litigation Hold; eDiscovery hold; Microsoft 365 and Office 365 retention policies; Mailbox audit logging; Calendar logging

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The Purges subfolder is not visible to end users.
claims.quote: Purges: If either Litigation Hold or single item recovery is enabled, this subfolder contains all items that are hard deleted. This folder isn't visible to end users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The Versions subfolder is not visible to end users.
claims.quote: The original copy is saved in the Versions subfolder. This process is known as copy-on-write page protection. Copy-on-write page protection applies to items residing in any mailbox folder. The Versions subfolder isn't visible to users.

claims.claim: In-Place Hold or Litigation Hold stops automatic Managed Folder Assistant purging of DiscoveryHolds, Deletions and Purges.
claims.quote: Putting a mailbox on In-Place Hold or Litigation Hold stops the Managed Folder Assistant from automatically purging messages from the DiscoveryHolds, Deletions, and Purges subfolders.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Users cannot delete items when the Recoverable Items quota is reached.
claims.quote: If the Recoverable Items folder for a mailbox reaches the Recoverable Items quota, no more items can be stored in the folder. ... Mailbox users can't delete items.

claims.claim: At the Recoverable Items quota, the Managed Folder Assistant cannot delete items based on retention tags.
claims.quote: The Managed Folder Assistant can't delete items based on retention tag or managed folder settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises assessing Recoverable Items consumption using each folder's FolderSize rather than FolderAndSubfolderSize.
claims.quote: When you evaluate Recoverable Items folder consumption, use the FolderSize value for each Recoverable Items folder returned by Get-MailboxFolderStatistics. Don't rely on FolderAndSubfolderSize

claims.claim: Moving an item to Recoverable Items deducts its size from the mailbox quota.
claims.quote: When an item is moved to the Recoverable Items folder, its size is deducted from the mailbox quota

claims.claim: Moving an item to Recoverable Items adds its size to that folder's consumption.
claims.quote: its size is deducted from the mailbox quota and added to the size of the Recoverable Items folder (quota available is reduced).

claims.claim: Learn gives a default Exchange Online Recoverable Items soft limit of 20 GB.
claims.quote: In Exchange Online, the default limits for the Recoverable Items quota are: a soft limit of 20 GB and a hard limit of 30 GB.

claims.claim: Learn gives a default Exchange Online Recoverable Items hard limit of 30 GB.
claims.quote: In Exchange Online, the default limits for the Recoverable Items quota are: a soft limit of 20 GB and a hard limit of 30 GB.

claims.claim: Litigation Hold, In-Place Hold or an applicable Microsoft 365 or Office 365 retention policy automatically raises the stated baseline quotas to 90 GB and 100 GB.
claims.quote: the quotas for the Recoverable Items folder are automatically increased to 90 GB and 100 GB, respectively, when you place a mailbox on Litigation Hold or In-Place Hold or if a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 retention policy is applied to the mailbox.
claims.fix: Retain these baseline figures but add the same page's archiving qualification: when archiving is enabled for a user on hold or assigned a retention policy, the primary mailbox's Recoverable Items warning quota rises to 95 GB and storage quota to 105 GB. The briefing recommends considering archiving, so distinguish its quotas.

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell can identify mailboxes on hold or show their assigned retention policy.
claims.quote: $MailboxesOnHold = Get-Mailbox -ResultSize unlimited | Where-Object {($_.InPlaceHolds -ne $null) -or ($_.LitigationHoldEnabled -eq "True")}

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Archive configuration and a custom Recoverable Items retention tag are documented responses to storage pressure on mailboxes on hold.
claims.quote: When the storage quota for the Recoverable Items folder in the primary mailbox of a mailbox on hold is close to reaching its limit, you can do the following things: ... Enable the archive mailbox and turn on auto-expanding archiving.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Content subject to a hold is intentionally preserved, and cleanup must respect that preservation.
claims.quote: you'll want to preserve the mailbox data until the hold is removed or single item recovery is disabled. In this case, you need to perform more detailed steps to clean up the Recoverable Items folder.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the governance checklist asks administrators to inspect.
claims.quote: Identify mailboxes on Litigation Hold, In-Place Hold or a retention policy, using Exchange Online PowerShell ... decide whether the archive mailbox and a retention policy tag ... fit your holds. Controls: display visibility, folder sizes, moving aged items.
claims.fix: Add documented rows for checking mailbox hold/retention status and archive-mailbox enablement, or narrow the checklist to the controls already in the table. The retention tag creation row is not a substitute for checking whether a mailbox's archive is enabled.

claims.claim: A Recoverable Items retention policy tag moves aged items from the primary mailbox's Recoverable Items folder to the archive mailbox's Recoverable Items folder.
claims.quote: This RPT moves items from the Recoverable Items folder in the user's primary mailbox to the Recoverable Items folder in the user's archive mailbox.
